_comment: Mutation testing on src/core only (ADR-0008). Coverage proves a line ran; it says nothing about whether an assertion would have noticed it being wrong, and for a bijection with no database that gap is the entire risk.
thresholds_comment: Calibrated on the measured run-to-run spread, on the machine that enforces it (ADR-0013); the runs are in issue #6. Only `break` decides the exit code, and it fires on `score < break` unrounded. The scored denominator is fixed by the mutant set, so the score moves in whole survivors: `break` is set to tolerate several times the largest spread ever observed, which is a few survivors, while still failing on a regression an order of magnitude smaller than the previous value could detect. `low` equals `break` so the report turns red exactly when the build breaks rather than colouring a nearly-breaking score green, and `high` sits above the whole observed range so green means `within noise of the floor`. Stryker validates only `high >= low`, so a `break` above `low` would be accepted silently and is what this avoids.
timeout_comment: Some mutants make a sampling loop run forever (turning `if (candidate < limit) return candidate` into `if (false)` is one). A timeout counts as killed, which is right — a test that never finishes has noticed. The deadline is `timeoutFactor * netTime + timeoutMS` per mutant, where netTime is the dry run time of that mutant's own covering tests, not of the suite (mutant-test-planner.ts). The key has to end in `_comment` or Stryker discards it with a warning (options-validator.ts); `_comment_timeout` did, on every run.
